chapter: Pranks, the Mingus fight and Duke's writing
title: Tizol's version of the Mingus confrontation
summary: Tizol says the story is lies: a quarrel over raising a bass part an octave led to threats, Mingus grabbed an iron bar and was fired.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Really, part of that, that's a bunch of stories; that's not the way it was.
That's a bunch of lies.

A bunch of lies is right. What really happened; this little piece of music that I wrote for him was nothing that I wrote; I got that from a little legit opera or thing from an a symphony or something, whatever it was.

So I ask him about it, and he took his bass down; he was practicing, I think, downstairs, and I went down there and I showed him, and said, "Try to play this to see what it sounds like on the bass", and he tried and so forth, and he wanted to raise it an octave higher. I said, "I don't want that. If I wanted to write it for a cello, I would have wrote it for a cello! I want to hear this on the bass".

So apparently, he got insulted or something. I said, "Well, go ahead and do what you want. I'm going upstairs to my dressing room". So he followed me upstairs to tell me, what's this and the other and so forth; I don't know; he raised a lot of hell, so by the time it came for
the show, I went downstairs, and he was still hot and said he was going to kick me in the behind, you know? "I should kick your behind". I said, "You gonna do what?" and he repeated it.

So I said, "Well, I tell you what I'm gonna do; I'm gonna go upstairs and when I come back, I would like for you to kick me right in the behind", and I went upstairs and when I came down, he thought I had a knife. And he grabbed one of those big pieces of iron that holds curtains and so forth, and he got it in his hand, and I remember, because Carney said, "Watch out, Juan, he's got a piece of iron!"
But he was still thinking that I had a knife, you know, and I didn't have a knife.
Uh huh. I think you told me yesterday that you usually did have one with you, but you didn't have one at this particular time.

Well, I used to sometimes carry a knife with me, you know? Because you can never tell, especially around Harlem or somewhere like that; somebody might want to do something after the show, someone could stop you, on the street, on 26th Street, on the way to the subway, and something might happen, so I would always carry a knife.
But not all the time. No, I didn't carry a knife all the time. So, after he went upstairs, after these things happened, after the show, he went upstairs and I was

upstairs in my dressing room, and I was so nervous, I was crying, you know? And he came up there, and the manager was there at the door of my dressing room, and when he came up there, he still wanted to keep saying something; I don't know it was what, but he wanted to keep on arguing about it with me.

And, I didn't respond or anything; I stayed right like that in my dressing room, and Celley was there trying to hold him back, you know? So, Duke came over -- I don't know how, but he told Celley to throw him out; to give him his two weeks notice and pay him off and let him go.
So he came back again -- he said, 'Juan, you made me lose my job' and so forth, and I said, 'Well, I can't help it -- you started it'. That was about the end of it.
Did he chase him or did he chase you across the stage? Because that's what he says here.

No, I came down to start the show, you know, to start the show. I came down there, and when he started to tell me, 'I'm going to kick your behind,' that's when he said that. So, when he said that, I said, 'Well, I'm going upstairs and when I come back I want for you to kick my behind', you know? So I guess he thought I went upstairs to do something or to get something, you know?
Uh huh.
When I came down, I thought I had a knife there in my room, or in my clothes, but I didn't have anything.

And when I came down, I guess he thought that I had a knife in my hand, so he grabbed this piece of iron and wanted to protect himself with a piece of iron. When he did that, Carney said, "Watch out --he's got a piece of iron in his hand" -- so one of the fellows -- one of the stagehands came back there and grabbed him, you know, and stopped it.
That's when Duke asked him to give his notice, and told Selle to pay him off.
